The paper does **not** report any taxadiene titer in *S. marcescens* — taxadiene has not been produced in this host according to the review.

Taxadiene is mentioned only once, as a prospective (not yet realized) target: the authors note that the repertoire of heterologous compounds currently producible in *S. marcescens* remains relatively limited, and that given its strong precursor supply and tolerance to hydrophobic products, there is "untapped potential" for fatty acid derivatives, polyketides, and longer-chain terpenoids "(e.g., taxadiene, squalene, β-carotene)" (p. 11).

The heterologous terpenoids with actual reported titers in *S. marcescens* HBQA7 are, for example, (−)-α-bisabolol at 102.3 g L⁻¹, (E)-nerolidol at 70.50 g L⁻¹, β-caryophyllene at 60.32 g L⁻¹, α-pinene at 32.5 g L⁻¹, S-(+)-linalool at 27.2 g L⁻¹, (S)-limonene at 22.8 g L⁻¹, geraniol at 25.12 g L⁻¹, and 1,8-cineole at 10.2 g L⁻¹ (Table 2, p. 9; text pp. 10–11).
